notes:
Binomial Theorem for a positive integer $n$

  • $(a+b)^n = \displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{n} {}^nC_r\,a^{n-r}b^r = {}^nC_0a^n + {}^nC_1a^{n-1}b + \cdots + {}^nC_nb^n$.
  • Total number of terms in the expansion $= n+1$.
  • Sum of all binomial coefficients: $^nC_0+{}^nC_1+\cdots+{}^nC_n = 2^n$ (put $a=b=1$).
  • Sum of coefficients at odd positions = sum at even positions $= 2^{n-1}$ (put $a=1,b=-1$).

General term

  • $T_{r+1} = {}^nC_r\,a^{n-r}b^r$ (the $(r+1)$th term, so $r=0$ gives the first term).
  • To find a specific term (e.g. term containing $x^k$), set the power of the variable in $T_{r+1}$ equal to $k$ and solve for $r$.

Middle term(s)

CaseMiddle term(s)
$n$ evensingle middle term $= T_{(n/2)+1}$
$n$ oddtwo middle terms $= T_{(n+1)/2}$ and $T_{(n+3)/2}$

Useful expansions

  • $(1+x)^n = 1+nx+\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}x^2+\cdots$ (for small $x$, $(1+x)^n \approx 1+nx$).
  • $(a+b)^n + (a-b)^n = 2[T_1+T_3+T_5+\cdots]$ (even-position original terms); $(a+b)^n - (a-b)^n = 2[T_2+T_4+\cdots]$.

Pascal's triangle

  • Row $n$ gives coefficients $^nC_0, {}^nC_1,\ldots,{}^nC_n$; each entry is the sum of the two entries above it (Pascal's rule).

Common tricks

  • Greatest binomial coefficient: for even $n$, it is $^nC_{n/2}$; for odd $n$, the two equal largest are $^nC_{(n-1)/2}$ and $^nC_{(n+1)/2}$.
  • To find the term independent of $x$, set the net power of $x$ in $T_{r+1}$ to 0.

Exam tip

KCET typically asks 1–2 questions from this chapter, usually finding a general/middle term, the term independent of $x$, or using $a=1,b=\pm1$ to evaluate a sum of binomial coefficients. Always write the general term formula first and substitute carefully — sign and power errors are the most common mistakes.

The coefficient of $x^7$ in the expansion of $\left(x^2 + \dfrac{2}{x}\right)^{11}$ is
questions.explanation: $T_{r+1} = {}^{11}C_r(x^2)^{11-r}\left(\dfrac2x\right)^r = {}^{11}C_r 2^r x^{22-3r}$. Setting $22-3r=7$ gives $r=5$; the coefficient is $^{11}C_5\,2^5 = 462\times32 = 14784$.

questions.explanation: Since $n=7$ is odd, two middle terms tie for the greatest coefficient: $^7C_3 = {}^7C_4 = 35$, corresponding to the 4th and 5th terms.

questions.explanation: Odd-power terms cancel and even-power terms double, leaving powers $0,2,4,6,8,10$ — a total of 6 terms.
